transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I've just completed your post-cataract surgery follow-up check. 

Do you have any questions about your surgery or your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! Yes, I do have a few questions. Firstly, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Great question! You can start doing light gardening after 1 week following your surgery. However, you should avoid any strenuous or heavy exercise for about a month.

So gentle gardening is fine, but try to steer clear of anything too demanding for that first month.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for that information! My next question is, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Good question! If you were using eye gel or drops for dry eyes before your surgery, it's safe to continue using them unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

So you can go ahead and use it as you normally would. Just make sure you store it as directed on the bottle - some need to be kept in the fridge and others at room temperature.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do. I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to check it further. In that case, please let your care team know.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, one more. Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That depends on how long it's been since your surgery. It's quite common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after your operation, but it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

If your vision is still blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything's okay.

How long ago was your surgery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: It's been about a week since my surgery.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's helpful to know. Since it's only been about a week, some blurriness is quite normal at this stage. Your vision should improve quickly over the coming days and weeks.

Just keep an eye on it, and if it gets significantly worse or doesn't improve as expected, let your care team know so we can check it.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, that's all for now. Thank you so much for the information!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're welcome! Just to confirm - have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, they have. Thanks again for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! Take care, and wishing you a smooth recovery.

verdict.label: pass
